findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync path returns a native `Response`, but Google reads `res.data`; refresh fails and the swallowed error leaves stale authorization.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — The entire Zod `{ success, data }` wrapper is persisted as `Credential.key`, breaking subsequent schema validation and service construction.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — A native `Response` is treated as a decoded `HubspotToken`; token fields become undefined and failures are only logged, silently breaking refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — Computed schema keys do not accept arbitrary fields, so expiry is stripped and a fake refresh-token sentinel is persisted, causing repeated refreshes and preventing later local refresh.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — The refreshed token is persisted, but the returned connection still uses the old token; sync parsing can also strip `instance_url`, breaking current and later operations.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7 — The documented shared-endpoint response contract is incompatible with callers expecting Gaxios, decoded HubSpot, nested Lark, or provider-specific Webex shapes; no single conforming response works across integrations.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The external sync request has no timeout or abort signal, so a hung service can block token refresh and synchronous availability/booking operations.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Separate `findFirst` and `create` calls make webhook delivery non-idempotent under retries or concurrency, producing duplicate and stale credentials.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — No request-level test covers missing webhook-secret configuration, leaving the unauthenticated credential-write path undetected.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Persisting the Zod result wrapper can make the current refresh appear successful while corrupting the database value and disabling subsequent Google Calendar operations.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The shared Fetch response conflicts with Google and HubSpot SDK response assumptions; both paths suppress the resulting failure and return control without usable credentials.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — The malformed Zod schema strips expiry values, causing Office 365 to repeatedly refresh and potentially create a request storm against the shared endpoint.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Concurrent initial deliveries can both create credentials; later updates and reads may select different duplicate rows.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — Any accepted team member can create shared credentials because the team branch bypasses the admin-access check.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Body validation, decryption, and JSON errors become HTTP 500 responses rather than stable 4xx contract errors, encouraging retries of invalid requests.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Expected malformed-payload failures are not translated to 4xx responses, causing futile webhook retries and misleading operational alerts.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — Refresh success relies on optional `statusText === "OK"` instead of HTTP status and discards provider error details, rejecting valid responses and obscuring failures.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — No tests exercise the routing matrix or real response shapes across sync settings, credential ownership, providers, and non-2xx responses.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — No tests cover user/team ownership branches, malformed state, rejected membership, or accepted non-admin membership across migrated callbacks.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The abstraction uses `any` while returning mutually incompatible transport shapes, allowing provider response mismatches to compile and fail only during refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 — The helper throws on failure yet returns the full `safeParse` result, producing inconsistent caller handling and accidental persistence of Zod envelopes.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — There is no event/version ordering guard or atomic upsert; replayed or delayed webhooks can overwrite newer credentials, while concurrent deliveries create duplicates.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — A slow sync endpoint can indefinitely hold token-dependent operations for all synced users, cascading one dependency failure across integrations.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Authentication fails open when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset because the missing header and environment value are both `undefined`, permitting unauthenticated credential writes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app-credential.ts lines 22-27: The check compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the check passes and the request proceeds. However, there's a prior check on line 17-19 that checks `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and returns 403. The APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED constant would need to be true for the code to reach the webhook secret check. Looking at the .env.example, CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to empty string "", not undefined. If the env var is set to empty string, then the comparison would be `undefined !== ""` which would correctly fail. But if the env var is completely unset (not in .env at all), both would be undefined and the check would pass. This is a real authentication bypass vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Sync requests contain only guessable user/app identifiers and no caller authentication, potentially exposing arbitrary users’ access tokens from a public sync service.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, it sends a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There's no authentication header, secret, or signature included in this outbound request. The finding claims this could expose arbitrary users' access tokens from a public sync service. However, this is an OUTBOUND request from Cal.com TO an external sync endpoint that the self-hoster controls. The security of that endpoint is the responsibility of whoever operates it. The webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) that RECEIVES credentials does have authentication via CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header check. The refreshOAuthTokens function is making a request to get tokens, not exposing them. The external service would need to authenticate the request, but that's outside Cal.com's control. This is a design choice for self-hosters to implement their own auth on their sync endpoint, not necessarily a vulnerability in this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is unsigned caller-controlled JSON without nonce or session binding, enabling account-linking CSRF and forged state fields such as `teamId`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for encodeOAuthState.ts, it only shows a file rename and import path change (from '../types' to '../../types'). The actual OAuth state encoding logic is not shown in the diff - the function implementation is not visible. The finding claims the OAuth state is unsigned and lacks nonce/session binding, but this is about existing code behavior, not something introduced by this diff. The diff only moves files to a new directory structure. Without seeing the actual implementation being changed, this finding is speculation about pre-existing code rather than a problem introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7 — The documented shared-endpoint response contract is incompatible with callers expecting Gaxios, decoded HubSpot, nested Lark, or provider-specific Webex shapes; no single conforming response works across integrations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural issue. Looking at the diff, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw response from the external endpoint when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true. However, different callers expect different response shapes: GoogleCalendarService expects res.data with access_token/expiry_date, HubspotCalendarService expects a HubspotToken object, LarkCalendarService expects a fetch Response that needs handleLarkError processing, and Office365 expects a response that needs handleErrorsJson. The function returns a generic fetch Response from the sync endpoint, but callers like Google try to access res.data.access_token directly, which would fail on a raw fetch Response. This is a real type/contract mismatch that would cause runtime errors when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The external sync request has no timeout or abort signal, so a hung service can block token refresh and synchronous availability/booking operations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, lines 6-14 show a fetch call to process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without any timeout, AbortController, or signal configuration. This is a real issue because if the external credential sync endpoint hangs or is slow to respond, it will block the token refresh operation indefinitely. This could cause availability checks and booking operations to hang, affecting user experience. The fetch API by default has no timeout, so this is a legitimate concern for production code making external HTTP requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Separate `findFirst` and `create` calls make webhook delivery non-idempotent under retries or concurrency, producing duplicate and stale credentials.

adjudication.rationale: The code at lines 62-91 uses a findFirst followed by either update or create. This is indeed a race condition - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId/appId, both could execute findFirst before either creates, resulting in duplicate credentials. Additionally, if a retry happens, the same issue could occur. This is a real correctness problem with the upsert pattern implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — No request-level test covers missing webhook-secret configuration, leaving the unauthenticated credential-write path undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about missing test coverage for a specific code path. This is a test coverage concern, not a bug or security issue in the actual code. The code itself correctly checks for the webhook secret and returns 403 if it doesn't match. The absence of tests is a quality/process concern but not a 'real problem' in the code itself - the authentication logic is implemented correctly. This is essentially a test coverage nit rather than a defect in the production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Persisting the Zod result wrapper can make the current refresh appear successful while corrupting the database value and disabling subsequent Google Calendar operations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, line 97 in GoogleCalendarService.ts shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then `data: { key }` is used in the prisma update. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function returns the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` which is a Zod SafeParseReturnType object containing `{success: boolean, data?: T, error?: ZodError}`, not the actual parsed data. This means the credential key field would be set to the wrapper object instead of the actual credential data, which would corrupt the database and break subsequent operations. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The shared Fetch response conflicts with Google and HubSpot SDK response assumptions; both paths suppress the resulting failure and return control without usable credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, refreshOAuthTokens returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) or the result of refreshFunction(). For Google Calendar (line 86-92), the code expects res?.data.access_token and res?.data.expiry_date. When using the credential sync endpoint, a raw fetch Response is returned, which doesn't have a .data property - you'd need to call response.json() first. Similarly for HubSpot, the code expects hubspotRefreshToken to be a HubspotToken object with properties like accessToken, but a raw fetch Response would be returned instead. This is a real type mismatch that would cause the code to fail when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — The malformed Zod schema strips expiry values, causing Office 365 to repeatedly refresh and potentially create a request storm against the shared endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts file, the minimumTokenResponseSchema is indeed malformed. The schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed property names, which would evaluate to literal strings like '[object Object]' or similar, not dynamic property matching. This is not valid Zod syntax for matching arbitrary properties. However, the schema does correctly require `access_token: z.string()`. The claim about 'stripping expiry values' is partially valid - the schema doesn't properly capture expiry fields. But the more critical issue is that this schema syntax is fundamentally broken and won't work as intended. The function returns the parsed result which would fail validation for most real token responses. However, the code falls back to the provided schema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false, so this only affects the credential sharing feature. The finding identifies a real bug in the schema definition that could cause issues when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Concurrent initial deliveries can both create credentials; later updates and reads may select different duplicate rows.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app-credential.ts lines 56-77, the logic is: first findFirst to check if credential exists, then either update or create. In a race condition where two concurrent requests arrive for the same userId+appId combination, both could execute findFirst before either creates, both get null, and both proceed to create duplicate credentials. This is a real TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition that could result in duplicate credential rows. The code comment even acknowledges 'Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential' but upsert with a unique constraint would actually solve this. This is a legitimate concurrency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — Any accepted team member can create shared credentials because the team branch bypasses the admin-access check.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for createOAuthAppCredential.ts, it only shows import path changes (lines 6-7 changing from '../decodeOAuthState' to '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' and similar). The actual logic of the function is not shown in the diff - the file was renamed from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts with only import path updates. The finding claims there's a security issue at line 30 where team members can bypass admin-access checks, but the diff doesn't show any changes to the authorization logic - only the file relocation and import path updates. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Expected malformed-payload failures are not translated to 4xx responses, causing futile webhook retries and misleading operational alerts.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 31 in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts: `const reqBody = appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);`. The `z.parse()` method throws a ZodError when validation fails, but there's no try-catch around it. This means malformed payloads will result in an unhandled exception, which typically returns a 500 error instead of a 400 Bad Request. This is a real issue - the webhook endpoint should return a 4xx status for client errors (malformed input) rather than 5xx (server errors). This causes incorrect error categorization and could lead to unnecessary retry attempts by webhook senders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The abstraction uses `any` while returning mutually incompatible transport shapes, allowing provider response mismatches to compile and fail only during refresh.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the function signature is `async (refreshFunction: () => any, appSlug: string, userId: number | null)` and returns `any`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 — The helper throws on failure yet returns the full `safeParse` result, producing inconsistent caller handling and accidental persistence of Zod envelopes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the function does `safeParse`, then throws if `!refreshTokenResponse.success`, and then returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the full SafeParseReturnType object). The callers in the diff (GoogleCalendarService.ts line 95, Office365CalendarService.ts line 264) use the returned value. In GoogleCalendarService, it's assigned directly to `key` and passed to prisma update. In Office365CalendarService, it accesses `.success` and `.data` properties. The issue is that after the throw check, the function returns the SafeParseReturnType which has `.data` property, not the actual data. The Office365 caller handles this correctly by accessing `.data`, but GoogleCalendarService assigns the whole result object to `key` which would include the Zod envelope structure (`{success: true, data: {...}}`), not just the credential data. This is a real bug - the return type is inconsistent and GoogleCalendarService would store the wrong structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — There is no event/version ordering guard or atomic upsert; replayed or delayed webhooks can overwrite newer credentials, while concurrent deliveries create duplicates.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 56-77, the code does a findFirst to check if a credential exists, then either updates or creates. This is indeed a race condition - two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app could both pass the findFirst check (both finding no existing credential) and then both attempt to create, potentially resulting in duplicates. Additionally, there's no timestamp or version checking, so an older webhook processed after a newer one could overwrite fresher credentials. This is a real concurrency/race condition issue in the webhook handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — A slow sync endpoint can indefinitely hold token-dependent operations for all synced users, cascading one dependency failure across integrations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural concern in the new refreshOAuthTokens function. Looking at the code at lines 5-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, the function makes a fetch call to an external endpoint with no timeout configured. If this endpoint is slow or unresponsive, it will block the token refresh operation indefinitely. This affects all calendar integrations (Google, Office365, Lark, Hubspot) that use this function, meaning a single slow/failing sync endpoint could cascade failures across all OAuth token refreshes. However, this is more of a design/resilience concern than a clear bug - the code will work correctly when the endpoint responds normally. The lack of timeout is a valid concern but could be considered a missing feature rather than a defect.
